title: Introduce KMS token entropy separation and anonymous-audit-proxy for privacy-preserving residency claims
author: Jonah Kim
release_notes: Adds an opt-in anonymous audit proxy and KMS token entropy separation layer to limit disclosure of tenant residency while preserving cryptographic provenance. No user-facing API changes unless enabled by config; admin feature flag required for private deployments.
commits: a1f3b2e: implement initial token splitter service and unit tests
b4d2c3a: wire anonymous audit proxy into audit pipeline and add config options
c9f7e11: add RBAC gate for attribute-based residency disclosure and integration tests
d2a7b9c: docs and deployment notes, feature-flag gating for private installer
description:
Motivation: We have multiple customer requests for minimizing residency-sensitive metadata in audit copies while retaining cryptographic KMS-backed provenance for forensic needs. Current audit headers leak precise KMS region and tenant identifiers during cross-system replication (e.g. when forwarding to partner logging or long-term archives). This PR introduces a privacy-preserving shim that separates KMS token entropy (for signature verification) from clear-text residency claims and an anonymous-audit-proxy that can be deployed in edge/outbound pipelines. The goal is to give teams an opt-in knob to avoid exposing tenant location claims to downstream systems while keeping strong provenance for Redwoods' internal auditors.

Summary of changes and approach: This change implements three coordinated pieces: (1) token-splitter service in infra/kms that derives two artifacts from a KMS-signed token: a verifier token (low-entropy, cryptographic proof) and an optional residency-claim blob (high-entropy, encrypted). (2) anonymous-audit-proxy that strips or replaces residency headers when forwarding audit events, retaining only the verifier token plus a per-tenant pseudonym. (3) RBAC v2 attribute gate: a fine-grained policy check that controls which internal actors are allowed to request the full residency-claim blob. The default behaviour is conservative: residency claims are redacted for all forwarded audit streams unless an allowlist is configured.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (docs/security/privacy/kms-anon-audit.md) with threat model and compatibility notes
- [x] Token-splitter implementation + unit tests (infra/kms/token-splitter)
- [x] Anonymous audit proxy + integration tests (services/audit/anonymous-proxy)
- [x] RBAC v2 gate (pkg/rbac/v2/attribute_gate.go) and policy examples
- [x] Feature flag and private-installer notes for Private deployments
- [x] E2E smoke: audit-forwarding to S3-compatible sink with redaction verification

Design highlights and security rationale: 
- Token entropy separation: the token-splitter produces a small verifier token (ECDSA-like proof) that verifies the event origin and integrity but contains no region/tenant cleartext. The encrypted residency-claim blob is stored/forwarded only when explicitly requested by an actor with RBAC privileges. This prevents accidental leakage in multi-tenant pipelines and partner forwards.
- Anonymous pseudonyms: audit events forwarded through the proxy carry a stable pseudonym per tenant (HMAC-based, key-rotatable) so that downstream analytics can correlate events without learning tenant identity or location.
- RBAC integration: the attribute gate checks (a) caller role, (b) purpose (audit-retrieval vs operational troubleshooting), and (c) residency policy (customer-level residency flags). Policies are evaluated synchronously; policy decisions are logged with non-sensitive context.

Files changed (high level): 
- infra/kms/token-splitter/service.go: new microservice that interfaces with KMS wrappers and issues verifier tokens and encrypted claim blobs. Includes unit tests and a small shim to support local testing with dev KMS emulation.
- services/audit/anonymous-proxy/middleware.go: HTTP middleware that rewrites headers, validates verifier tokens, and replaces tenant identifiers with pseudonyms. Graceful bypass mode implemented for internal-only streams.
- services/audit/anonymous-proxy/config.yaml: new config with allowlists, retention windows, and pseudonym key rotation parameters.
- pkg/rbac/v2/attribute_gate.go: RBAC gate logic plus unit tests; integrates with policy compiler to accept new attributes: purpose and residency_request.
- docs/security/privacy/kms-anon-audit.md: design doc, rollout instructions, and operational runbook for incident scenarios where full residency claims are required.

Testing and CI: Full unit test coverage added for token-splitter (85%+) and RBAC gate (90%+). Integration tests added to the audit service CI matrix to exercise header rewrite and verifier token acceptance. CI initially flaked in the integration stage due to a race in the local KMS emulator; fixed by adding a backoff and explicit wait in tests. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (abridged): 
- Aisha Patel (reviewer): "Can we ensure the verifier token uses a domain-separated signature to avoid cross-compat issues with existing service tokens? Also request explicit migration notes for existing audit consumers." 
- Jonah (author): "Added domain separation to the signer and included migration notes in the docs. The anon-proxy exposes a compatibility mode that emits the original headers for allowed internal sinks behind a network ACL." 
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): "How does key rotation affect existing pseudonyms? Will rotation break analytics?" 
- Jonah: "Pseudonyms are HMAC over tenant-id || rotation-epoch; analytics teams should be advised of rotation windows. Docs include guidance and a migration script for re-hashing existing datasets if customers opt into re-identification." 
- Rae Thompson (security reviewer): "Threat model looks good; ensure we log policy decisions but not the residency-claim blob itself. Also add alerting for anomalous requests to retrieve full claims." 
- Jonah: "Added audit hooks and an alerting recipe in the runbook. Retrieval requests now increment a guarded metric and require two-person approval in the UI for Private installs."

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (opt-in, internal): deploy anon-proxy to audit-forwarding path for non-prod pipelines, monitor metrics and false-positive redaction rates for 72h.
- Phase 2 (opt-in, customer): expose feature flag to Private customers behind support ticket; include migration assistance for analytics teams.
- Phase 3 (guarded default): after customer feedback, consider toggling to default redact-forwards for partner-facing sinks; will require release notes and Opt-Out instructions.

Operational notes and SLO impact: Redaction path adds negligible latency (~2-6ms p95) measured in our test harness. Key management increases KMS calls only when residency-claim blobs are requested; default path avoids extra KMS calls. We added telemetry to track additional KMS ops and proxy CPU. No changes to user-rate limits.

Backward compatibility: The change is opt-in; no existing public API surface is modified. For Hosted customers we will not enable the proxy by default until we have validated partner behaviours. Private installers have a new config boolean (enable_anonymous_audit_proxy) and a migration checklist in the docs.

Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4321): 
- Add a CLI tool to re-map pseudonyms for historical archives (ENG-4321.2)
- Expand policy compiler examples to include per-customer residency exceptions (ENG-4321.3)
- Add SRE alerting runbook automations for queued residency-claim retrieval requests (ENG-4321.4)

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after reviewers approved. Please see commits listed above for original history.

If questions or you want to run the local emulation: follow docs/security/privacy/kms-anon-audit.md and use infra/kms/token-splitter/README.md for quickstart.
